recall_prompt: Say how you would find the 6th term — which r you use in the general term, and how the fractions cancel to a whole number.
insider_note: The 6th term is Tᵣ₊₁ with r = 5, not 6. The fractions are built to cancel — (2⁴/3⁴)(3⁵/2⁵) reduces to a single small fraction — so heavy arithmetic means a wrong r.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write T₆ from the general term
steps.margin_note: First mark. The 6th term is Tᵣ₊₁ with r = 5: ⁹C₅ times the first entry to the power 4 times the second to the power 5.
lines: In (x + y)ⁿ, Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ xⁿ⁻ʳ yʳ

recall.must_convey: That the 6th term is T₅₊₁ = ⁹C₅ (2x/3)⁴ (3y/2)⁵.
accept: the sixth term is r equal to five in the general term, nine C five into two x by three to the four into three y by two to the five
use T r plus one with r five
T six is nine C five two x by three power four three y by two power five
sixth term ante r five, nine C five two x by three power four three y by two power five
r is one less than six

steps.why: The r-th power of the second entry appears in the (r + 1)-th term, so the 6th term has r = 5.
common_mistakes: Giving the first entry the power 5.

steps.label: Cancel and evaluate

recall.must_convey: That ⁹C₅ = 126 and the fractions reduce to 3/2, so T₆ = 189 x⁴y⁵.
accept: nine C five is one twenty six, the fractions reduce to three by two, so the term is one eighty nine x to the four y to the five
the sixth term is one eighty nine x power four y power five
two to the four by three to the four times three to the five by two to the five is three by two
fractions cancel ayyi three by two, one twenty six into three by two one eighty nine
one hundred eighty nine x to the fourth y to the fifth

steps.why: The two fractions are almost reciprocals; one extra 3 on top and one extra 2 below survive, and 126 × 3/2 is a whole number.
